https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/04/moln.text: Menü Kereső Újabb civil szervezetekről derült ki, hogy jogosulatlanul kaphattak NKA-támogatást Belföld Németh-Halász Nikolett Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Molnár Áron öt újabb civil szervezetet mutatott be Facebook-oldalán, amik szerinte jogtalanul kaptak százmilliós NKA-támogatást. Az öt szervezetet Monor fideszes képviselőtestülete köti össze. Molnár Áron név szerint is megnevezte egyiküket, Dessewffy Andort, Monor fideszes alpolgármesterét, aki a „Közösségi Élet az Ezer Pince Városában” nevű alapítvány képviselője. Molnár Áron a videójához dokumentumokat is feltöltött, amiken az látszik, hogy a megnevezett alapítvány áprilisban még benyújtotta az elszámolást, majd májusban technikai és egyéb okok miatt úgy döntött, mégsem tud elszámolni. A dokumentumokból kiderül, hogy nemcsak megrendeltek, hanem ki is fizettek támogatásokat. Az egyik számla egy idén március 15-ei buszútra vonatkozik, az irány pedig Monorról Budapestre a Békemenetre és visszafele szólt. A színész szerint ez újabb bizonyíték arra, hogy a kultúrára fordítandó adófizetői forintokat fideszes rendezvényekre, kampányeseményekre költötték. Molnár Áron kijelentései miatt megkerestük Dessewffy Andort, ha reagál, beszámolunk róla. Hankó Balázs volt kulturális és innovációs miniszter idején a gyanú szerint az NKA állami kulturális pályázati forrásait úgy osztották el választókerületenként, hogy azokat a Fidesz választási kampányában lehessen felhasználni. Az ügyben eddig hét embert tartóztattak le, legutóbb Hankó Balázs volt kabinetfőnökét . Az egy hónappal ezelőtt letartóztatott hat ember közül négy maradt letartóztatásban, ketten hazatérhettek, de bűnügyi felügyelet alá kerültek. Hankó volt kabinetfőnökének letartóztatása után Magyar Péter miniszterelnök azt írta : Hankó Balázs néhány napig még megpróbálhat bebújni az általa utasított beosztottjai mögé, de a tettei következményét senki nem kerülheti el. Hankó Balázst országgyűlési képviselőként a mentelmi jog védi. Ha az ügyben nyomozó Bács-Kiskun Vármegyei Főügyészség meggyanúsítaná, ahhoz előbb ki kellene kérni a mentelmi jogát az Országgyűléstől. Hankó korábbi közleményében azt írta: „Nem próbálok elszökni, nem akadályozom a hatóságok munkáját, és együttműködöm velük. Nem követtem el bűncselekményt, de »bűnismétlésre« elvi lehetőségem sincs. Éppen ezért tartanám megalapozatlannak – csakúgy, mint volt kollégáimmal szemben – ha a legsúlyosabb kényszerintézkedést alkalmaznák olyan körülmények között, amikor annak törvényi feltételei nem állnak fenn.” Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! The legacy of the Nuremberg Trials To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video https://p.dw.com/p/5O2o6 Skip next section Germany to buy cruise missiles for mass deployment 10/09/2026 October 9, 2026 Germany to buy cruise missiles for mass deployment Germany's army has decided to acquire large numbers of low-cost cruise missiles capable of striking targets up to 1,500 kilometers (930 miles) away. Army chief Lieutenant General Christian Freuding announced the decision at a military gathering in Berlin, saying the weapons would be used to overwhelm enemy air defenses through sheer numbers. The move reflects lessons from the war in Ukraine, where drones and missiles have been deployed in large numbers to exhaust air defenses. Launching numerous relatively cheap weapons simultaneously can force defenders to expend expensive interceptor missiles, potentially allowing more sophisticated weapons to reach their targets. Germany plans to combine the cheaper missiles with more powerful weapons designed to strike strategically important targets, including US-made cruise missiles it intends to purchase . Freuding said the army was considering two commercially available systems, although neither had yet been approved for use by the German armed forces. Initial deliveries could begin in 2027. US defense company Covenant opened a cruise missile production facility in Leipzig earlier this week. It plans to manufacture 1,000 Anthem missiles in 2027 and 5,000 in 2028. The company says each missile would cost a six-figure sum, below €860,000 ($1 million), compared with several million dollars for conventional cruise missiles. https://p.dw.com/p/5O1qt Skip next section Heart attack deaths down 15% since 2022 10/09/2026 October 9, 2026 Heart attack deaths down 15% since 2022 Deaths from heart attacks in Germany fell by more than 15% between 2022 and 2025, according to figures released by the Federal Statistical Office. Deaths from cerebrovascular diseases, including strokes and brain hemorrhages, also declined by 6.3% over the same period. However, deaths from respiratory diseases rose by around 8% in 2025 compared with the previous year, reaching 81,200. Overall, Germany recorded around 1.01 million deaths in 2025, virtually unchanged from the previous year. The total was nevertheless 5.6% lower than in 2022. Despite the decline in heart attack and stroke-related deaths, cardiovascular disease remained Germany's leading cause of death, accounting for 334,100 deaths in 2025. Heart attack deaths fell among both men and women, with the sharpest decline, 30.6%, among people aged 80 to 85. It is not clear what is behind the decline. Changes in population size and age structure may have contributed, as the statistics are not adjusted for age. The figure rose from 62,000 the previous year and 56,000 two years earlier, continuing an upward trend that has raised concerns about educational standards and Germany's shortage of skilled workers. The proportion of students leaving school without at least a Hauptschulabschluss , Germany's basic secondary school qualification, reached 8.4% in 2024/2025. That compares with 6.6% in 2018/2019 and around 5.5% in 2013/2014. The latest rate is the highest recorded in 20 years, although it was even higher around the turn of the millennium. The number of school leavers without qualifications has also risen substantially over the past decade, from around 47,400 in 2014/2015. Numbers temporarily fell during the COVID-19 pandemic, potentially reflecting relaxed examination requirements, before beginning to climb again. Investigators say new information suggests that the remains of Kerstin Lee Langley, missing since the summer of 2007, could be buried in a meadow and woodland near the village of Kadenzhofen, north of Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz. Specialists from Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office and the Regensburg criminal police department are examining an area covering approximately 100 square meters (1,076 square feet). An excavator is removing soil in layers, which investigators then examine for possible evidence. Police spokesperson Corinna Wild told public broadcaster BR24 that investigators were following specific information suggesting Langley's body could be buried at the site. Police told DW they had ruled out any connection between the search and a fatal shooting just a few kilometers away in the village of Berngau, where two local government employees were killed during a routine firearms inspection at around the same time on Thursday afternoon. https://p.dw.com/p/5O1Wk Skip next section How was the Berngau suspect arrested? 10/09/2026 October 9, 2026 How was the Berngau suspect arrested? Police have yet to establish a motive for the fatal shooting of two local government employees during the routine check in Berngau Image: Tizian Gerbing/dpa/picture alliance Police said a man who opened fire on local government employees in the southern town of Berngau barricaded himself inside his home and contacted their operations center by telephone. He admitted firing shots, said he had firearms in his possession and warned that he would not surrender without resistance. Special police units, including a tactical response team with an armored vehicle, were deployed to the village. A police helicopter was also used, while residents were advised to stay indoors or avoid the cordoned-off area. Negotiators spent hours trying to persuade the suspect to surrender peacefully. "We always try to achieve a peaceful solution, and that generally happens through communication," a police spokesperson said. However, at around 2:20 a.m. (0020 GMT/UTC) Friday, officers entered the building using explosives. Police said officers fired shots during the operation, lightly wounding the suspect in the leg. He was subsequently given medical treatment. Police have not yet established why the suspect allegedly opened fire on the two officials. Photograph: Beinvenido Velasco/EPA Panama Powerful 7.6-magnitude earthquake hits Panama and triggers tsunami warnings Hazardous waves are possible as far south as Ecuador and as far north as Mexico, as 13 aftershocks reported Guardian staff and agencies Fri 9 Oct 2026 17.58 EDT First published on Fri 9 Oct 2026 14.29 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the west coast of Central and South America, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS). The quake hit along the southern coast of the country, the USGS said. It was centered near the southern tip of the Central American country, about 14km (9 miles) south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said. The Institute of Geosciences of the University of Panama said the quake struck at just before 1pm local time near the southern town of Tonosí. The Panamanian institute said that a second 6.0 magnitude earthquake struck soon after, at 1.22pm. By 1.3opm there had reportedly been 13 aftershocks. The president, José Raúl Mulino, said he had asked a key minister to call for calm. “What happened should not be used to generate alarm and disorder,” Mulino wrote on X. Local newspaper La Prensa said that across the Central American country, buildings, schools and homes were evacuated as a result of the “powerful movement of the earth”. Footage published by La Prensa showed severe damage to several buildings in the city of Penonomé, including the St John Baptist Cathedral. Other photos showed a highway to the west of the capital that had been completely sheared in half by the earthquake. Tremors were felt strongly ​in the ⁠capital of ⁠Panama ​City, ‌according ‌to ‌witnesses who spoke to Reuters. The Associated Press reported that buildings shook and visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact. The USGS said hazardous waves were possible along the coasts of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico, although the tsunami warning for Chile was cancelled at 4.18pm local time. Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service said on the Telemetro Reporta news channel that damage was concentrated in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said there were no reports of damage in the capital, which is known for its hundreds of skyscrapers. Smith said several injuries had been reported, including one person struck by debris from a partially collapsed structure in the city of Penonomé, about 93 miles (150km) from the capital. He confirmed a partial collapse and cracks at the cathedral in the district’s main square, as well as damage in the governor’s office building and the Dos Continentes hotel. No casualties were immediately reported. Local news outlets also reported that the church of San Atanasio, a colonial-style Catholic church in Panama’s Los Santos province, had collapsed. The church was declared a National Historic Heritage Site in 1938. Elsewhere, including in Veraguas province, large fissures ran along roadways. Tocumen international airport in Panama City, one of the region’s busiest airports with more than 20 million travelers in 2025, said it would temporarily suspend operations and activated evacuation plans. It said operations would resume once security conditions had been checked. The Panama Canal Authority said operations were continuing normally along the key global trade route. It said its priority was the safety of employees, vessels and crews and that specialized technical teams were inspecting facilities for possible damage. Photograph: Jason O’Brien/AAP Queensland Police investigate gang links as woman, 19, dies after drive-by shooting at Brisbane pub Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau was injured during the shooting outside Fitzy’s Loganholme in the city’s south on Saturday Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Thu 29 Oct 2026 04.14 EDT First published on Thu 29 Oct 2026 03.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Potential gang involvement in the fatal drive-by shooting of a 19-year-old woman is being investigated by police. Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, from Jimboomba, was hit in the head and neck when masked gunmen opened fire into a crowd outside Fitzy’s Loganholme, a pub in Brisbane’s south, on Saturday night. She died in the Princess Alexandra hospital on Thursday morning. Three men, aged 27, 37 and 38, were also hospitalised. One is recovering from surgery while the other two have been released. Sign up for the Breaking News Australia email Police are searching for those responsible for the attack, which happened on a night when the venue was hosting a boxing event. Det Insp Ian Galpin was visibly emotional as he announced the young woman’s death to the media. He offered his condolences to Schuster-Togiatau’s family and friends, adding that about 80 police officers were involved in the murder investigation. “We will not stop until these people are identified and taken into custody,” he said. “I’d ask our community to reflect on the fact that a 19-year-old woman, in the prime of her life, was simply going out for a night out with friends and has had her life taken from her in the most cowardly way. “There are people out there who know exactly who was involved in this offence and exactly why this occurred. “I’m asking those people to be brave enough to come forward with that information.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | When needed Sign up to Breaking News Australia Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion Det Insp Galpin said the young victim’s family was “not doing well” and had requested their privacy be respected. “It’s an incredibly difficult time for them, I can’t imagine the hurt that they’re going through,” he said.
